programs.title: Land for Wildlife NSW
programs.summary: Free property assessment and habitat-management advice through regional providers, generally for land with at least 0.5 hectares of native vegetation.
programs.commitment: Voluntary and not legally binding. Registration does not change the property's legal status or put a covenant on title.
programs.funding: CEN's separate 2026–27 BCT grant allocation is fully allocated. Applications can join a waitlist; program registration itself remains available.

contacts.name: Border Ranges Richmond Valley Landcare Network

programs.title: Conservation Partners Agreements
programs.summary: BCT conservation support for eligible NSW landholders, generally with at least 20 hectares of native vegetation in moderate to good condition. Smaller high-value sites may be considered.
programs.commitment: Voluntary to enter, then permanent, registered on title and binding on future owners. Restrictions protect the agreed conservation area.
programs.funding: No annual management payments. Eligible agreement holders can separately apply for Conservation Partners Grants. Agreement expressions of interest follow regional timing.

programs.title: Wildlife Refuge Agreements
programs.summary: An entry-level agreement for eligible NSW landholders, generally with at least 10 hectares of native vegetation in moderate to good condition. Enquiries are accepted year-round.
programs.commitment: Registered on title and continues when land is sold, but can be revoked by the landholder. Conservation restrictions apply while it is in place.
programs.funding: No annual management payments. Eligible holders can apply separately for Conservation Partners Grants, subject to assessment and available funding.

programs.title: Biodiversity stewardship agreements
programs.summary: Eligible landholders can create biodiversity credits for sale. Assessment costs, credit demand and a site management plan determine suitability; a sale or financial return is not guaranteed.
programs.commitment: Designed for permanent conservation and registered on title, binding future owners with ongoing management and reporting duties. Review the limited termination provisions before signing.
programs.funding: The separate Stewardship Support Program closed on 13 September 2026; reopening is expected in 2027. The underlying stewardship pathway remains available.

programs.title: Big Scrub Rainforest Conservancy
programs.summary: Landholders in the Big Scrub footprint can enquire about restoration assistance and a possible inspection of suitable subtropical lowland rainforest sites.
programs.commitment: An enquiry starts a suitability discussion. The team asks about the property's location, area available for regeneration, vegetation and soil; inspections depend on suitability and available resources.
programs.funding: A support pathway, not an open cash grant. An enquiry does not guarantee an inspection, restoration work or funding. Ask the team about available assistance and any costs.

programs.title: Byron habitat restoration register
programs.summary: Byron Shire Council keeps a register of landholders interested in tree planting and habitat restoration, and contacts them when project funding becomes available.
programs.commitment: Contact Council's Biodiversity Team to register your interest. Council will discuss the requirements of any later project; registering does not guarantee selection.
programs.funding: An interest register, not a currently open grant. Assistance depends on future funding and project suitability. This is a Byron Shire pathway; landholders elsewhere should contact their own council.
